## Learning objectives

By the end of this tutorial, you should be able to:

- configure a Spring Boot application for MongoDB
- map an aggregate and embedded values to one BSON document
- use `MongoRepository` for CRUD and derived queries
- define indexes and translate a duplicate key into an HTTP response
- inspect Spring Data's result with `mongosh`
- decide when repository abstraction is enough and when lower-level APIs help

## From `mongosh` to Spring Data

Tutorial 11b made every database operation explicit. Spring Data keeps the
same MongoDB model but moves the mapping and routine access code into Java.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  Client[HTTP client] --> Controller[RentalController]
  Controller --> Repository[RentalRepository]
  Repository --> Mapping[Spring Data mapping]
  Mapping --> Mongo[(rentals collection)]
  Shell[mongosh] -. inspect .-> Mongo
```

The abstraction does not remove the need to understand documents, access
patterns, indexes, atomicity, or query plans.

## A deliberately isolated demonstration

The code lives in `training/demos/mongodb-spring-data` and does not import the
rental platform. It has one Spring Boot process, one MongoDB container, and one
aggregate.

| Component | Local port | Responsibility |
|---|---:|---|
| `rental-api` | 8093 | Create and query tutorial rentals |
| `mongodb` | 27018 | Store `rental_spring_training.rentals` |

Isolation lets us learn persistence APIs before outbox, messaging, projection,
and service integration enter the picture.

## Dependency and connection

```groovy
dependencies {
    implementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-web'
    implementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-data-mongodb'
}
```

```properties
spring.data.mongodb.uri=${SPRING_DATA_MONGODB_URI:mongodb://localhost:27018/rental_spring_training}
spring.data.mongodb.auto-index-creation=true
```

Spring Boot creates the MongoDB client, mapping converter, and repository
implementation. Environment variables replace the local URI in Compose.

## Map one aggregate to one document {.smaller}

```java
@Document(collection = "rentals")
public record Rental(
    @Id String id,
    @Indexed(unique = true) @Field("rental_id") String rentalId,
    @Indexed @Field("customer_id") String customerId,
    Vehicle vehicle,
    Status status,
    List<String> options,
    Price price,
    @Field("created_at") Instant createdAt) {

  public record Vehicle(
      @Field("plate_number") String plateNumber,
      String category) {}
  public record Price(BigDecimal amount, String currency) {}
}
```

`Vehicle` and `Price` are embedded because they belong to the rental aggregate.

## Java names and stored names

| Java | MongoDB | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `id` + `@Id` | `_id` | Technical document identity |
| `rentalId` | `rental_id` | Stable business identity |
| `customerId` | `customer_id` | Query field |
| `vehicle.plateNumber` | `vehicle.plate_number` | Nested value |
| `Instant` | BSON date | Time with a precise type |
| `BigDecimal` | Decimal128 | Decimal value without binary rounding |

Mapping annotations are a persistence contract. Renaming a Java property does
not migrate documents already stored in MongoDB.

## `MongoRepository`: generated CRUD

```java
public interface RentalRepository
    extends MongoRepository<Rental, String> {

  Optional<Rental> findByRentalId(String rentalId);

  List<Rental> findByCustomerIdAndStatus(
      String customerId, Rental.Status status);
}
```

Spring supplies `save`, `findById`, `findAll`, `deleteById`, and the
implementation of both declared methods. The method name becomes a query; it
does not automatically create the matching index.

## Save: insert or replace?

```java
Rental saved = repository.save(new Rental(
    null, request.rentalId(), request.customerId(), request.vehicle(),
    request.status(), request.options(), request.price(), Instant.now()));
```

- a null `@Id` normally produces an insert and MongoDB assigns `_id`;
- an existing `@Id` normally produces an update/replacement;
- business identity is protected separately by the unique `rental_id` index;
- blind `save` is not a substitute for domain validation or concurrency control.

Use an explicit service layer when business rules become more than mapping.

## Indexes express access and integrity

```java
@Indexed(unique = true)
@Field("rental_id")
String rentalId
```

The unique index prevents two documents from owning the same rental identity,
including concurrent requests. A second index on `customer_id` supports the
tutorial query, although a compound index may better match
`customer_id + status` at scale.

`auto-index-creation=true` is convenient for a lab. Production systems usually
manage index changes explicitly and observe their deployment cost.

## Persistence failures need API semantics

```java
@RestControllerAdvice
class ApiExceptionHandler {
  @ExceptionHandler(DuplicateKeyException.class)
  @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CONFLICT)
  Map<String, String> duplicateKey(DuplicateKeyException exception) {
    return Map.of("error", "A rental with this identifier already exists");
  }
}
```

MongoDB enforces the invariant; Spring translates the driver failure into
`DuplicateKeyException`; the API translates it into HTTP `409 Conflict`.
Do not expose database exception details to clients.

## Keep `mongosh` in the feedback loop

```javascript
use rental_spring_training
db.rentals.findOne({ rental_id: "RENT-42" })
db.rentals.getIndexes()
db.rentals.find({ customer_id: "CUSTOMER-7", status: "OPEN" })
          .explain("executionStats")
```

Inspect the real field names, BSON types, generated `_id`, and chosen query
plan. A repository method compiling successfully proves neither efficient
access nor correct persisted shape.

## Repository methods versus `MongoTemplate`

| Prefer repositories | Consider `MongoTemplate` |
|---|---|
| CRUD around aggregates | Dynamic or conditional queries |
| Stable derived queries | Partial updates with operators |
| Simple pagination | Custom aggregation pipelines |
| Domain-oriented interfaces | Fine control of query/update documents |

Both use the same mapping infrastructure. Use the smallest abstraction that
expresses the operation clearly; dropping lower does not make a query better
designed.

## Atomicity and transactions

- One MongoDB document is the natural atomic write boundary.
- Embedded values change atomically with their parent document.
- A repository call does not create a transaction spanning several documents.
- Multidocument transactions require a replica set and a
  `MongoTransactionManager`.

This tutorial intentionally needs no multidocument transaction. Module 12 adds
one because the insurance aggregate and its outbox intent must commit together.

## What Spring Data does—and does not do

Spring Data provides mapping, conversions, repository implementations,
exception translation, and integration with Spring transactions.

It does **not** choose aggregate boundaries, invent access patterns, guarantee
useful indexes, solve schema evolution, make distributed writes atomic, or
turn a mutable aggregate into a CQRS projection.

Continue with [Lab 11c](lab.md), then apply the concepts to the real
[insurance aggregate](../12-mongodb-aggregate-store/slides.qmd).
